first.rationale: Competitor pricing pressure makes promotional_pricing (memory_73) tempting, but that memory only supports 'acquisition and revenue lift' — it was never verified against sustainable, qualified long-term revenue (the current objective), and discount-driven signups risk attracting exactly the low-LTV price-sensitive accounts the competitor is targeting. Given only one experiment slot, chasing price competition now is high-consequence and under-verified for this objective, so I verify memory_73 first. Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, which is the more directly measurable and lower-risk lever; memory_31 and memory_86 support acting there, but memory_31 is older and narrower (SMB activation via field-cutting) so I also verify it to confirm it generalizes to the current onboarding completion drop rather than assuming durability. I intend to run a small guarded onboarding-simplification test this week, monitoring downstream conversion-to-paid and retention (not just completion rate) so a short-term completion bump doesn't mask lower-quality activations, while explicitly flagging promotional pricing as a live but unresolved option pending verification results.

final.rationale: Verification confirmed promotional_pricing (memory_73's source) is actively harmful to the primary objective: the discounted cohort produced +18% short-term qualified revenue but -12% 30-day retention and does not survive first renewal, so it is explicitly not a sustainable-growth strategy. That rules it out despite competitive pressure — chasing it would optimize a vanity metric while destroying long-term qualified revenue. Verification of memory_31 confirmed signup simplification holds for SMB with a modest but real qualified-revenue gain (+4%) and near-flat retention (-1%), directly addressing the current onboarding-completion decline with the least downstream risk of the untested options. I therefore commit the week's single experiment slot to a small guarded rollout of onboarding simplification targeted at SMB self-serve accounts, tracking activation, 30-day retention, and qualified revenue (not just completion) to catch any retention erosion early, and explicitly hold promotional_pricing and enterprise_sales_assist as unverified/rejected-for-now options rather than pursuing them this cycle.
